outlook: Grains ended a weak week mixed Friday. December corn fell 4½ cents to $4.56, a 3½-month low, and was down 18¼ cents on the week under harvest pressure despite a USDA flash sale of 116,000 tons to unknown destinations. November soybeans gained 3½ cents on short covering but still lost 4¾ cents for the week as harvest and farmer hedge selling capped gains. Wheat paused after another drop: Minneapolis December spring wheat slipped ¼ cent and lost 35 cents on the week, and Chicago wheat posted an eighth straight weekly loss — its longest losing run since 1997 — as the Black Sea risk premium faded, U.S. export sales lagged and Southern Hemisphere harvests advanced. Crude oil held above $100 a barrel on U.S.-Iran tensions, while canola traded near unchanged.
